Real-data deep dive · companion to pipeline_overview.html

Real Parse Data Validation — Findings & Scale Limits

The first four deep dives validated the pipeline against PBMC3k — droplet-based, one sample, a known-easy case. This one runs the full chain against a real 50,000-cell subset of Parse Biosciences' own published split-pool dataset (24 pooled donors), and reports what changed, including two findings that only show up at this scale.

Data: Parse 1M PBMC T1D (public, CC BY 4.0), 50k-cell real subset Scripts: 00 → 01 → 02 → 03 → 04, all real code, no shortcuts Full 987k-cell run: prepped on HiPerGator, not yet submitted
Data QC Clustering & the donor question Annotation at scale Next: full-scale HPC run References

01 · Data

What this run actually used

Parse Biosciences publishes a real Evercode dataset used in Seurat's own sketch-integration tutorial: 987,585 cells × 60,664 genes, 24 donors (12 healthy, 12 Type-1 diabetes), hosted publicly at cdn.parsebiosciences.com (CC BY 4.0, no login). The full matrix (1.18 billion non-zero entries, ~17GB to parse) was too large to safely load on this 32GB laptop, so validation here uses a real 50,000-cell subset — same files, same donors, same annotation quirks, just fewer rows. The full dataset is the target for the actual HPC run (see section 05).

Both pipeline entry points were exercised on this data: the direct DGE_filtered path and the simulated-Trailmaker Seurat-object path (Seurat::ReadParseBio() → .rds → 00b_seurat_to_dge_format.R → 00_load_parse_output.py) — both produced an identical 50,000 × 60,664 object.

02 · QC

QC held up on real data — with one genuine bug found and fixed

Real Parse gene annotation has ~1/3 of genes (20,055 of 60,664) with no gene_name — a blank CSV field, not a data artifact. This crashed the original loader (and, separately, crashed Seurat::ReadParseBio() too, with no fallback of its own). Fixed by falling back to gene_id for those genes. Full detail in the commit history; not re-derived here.

StageCells
Loaded50,000
After hard floors (200 genes/cell, 3 cells/gene)50,000
QC outliers (counts=153, genes=102, mito=602)−752
Predicted doublets−2,626
Final46,754 (93.5%)

Doublet rate (5.25%) is higher than PBMC3k's (1.2%), consistent with what the main doc already argues: split-pool doublet formation scales with cells loaded per sub-library, and this dataset pools far more cells per run than a single 10x lane.

03 · Clustering & the donor question

3–7 clusters became 9–22 — is that donors, or biology?

PBMC3k (one sample) produced 3–7 clusters across the resolution scan. This real, 24-donor-pooled dataset produced far more:

ResolutionClusters (real data)Clusters (PBMC3k)
0.293
0.4144
0.6206
0.8215
1.0227

No batch integration has been applied yet, so the obvious question is whether this is 24 donors' technical variation masquerading as clusters. Checked directly with Adjusted Rand Index (ARI) and Normalized Mutual Information (NMI) between leiden_r0.6 and donor identity:

MetricValue
ARI(clusters, donor)0.055
NMI(clusters, donor)0.176
Clusters >80% dominated by one donor1 / 20

Key result

Global agreement between clusters and donor identity is low (ARI 0.055) — the extra clusters are mostly not a batch-effect artifact. One cluster (16) is a clear exception at 95% single-donor composition, likely a donor-specific rare population or expanded clone, worth a manual look before trusting it. The most likely explanation for the rest: real biological richness at this scale (24 immune systems, ~50k cells) that a single 2,700-cell sample simply doesn't contain.

Still recommend batch integration before real comparative analysis

Low global ARI doesn't mean zero batch effect — cluster 16's single-donor dominance shows it exists locally. Harmony/scVI integration (already scoped as optional in the main doc, "once a real multi-sample run exists") should be applied before drawing conclusions that compare healthy vs. T1D donors specifically, even though the overall cluster structure looks trustworthy.

04 · Annotation at scale

The demo marker dictionary breaks down at 20 clusters

The markers/annotation deep dive already showed the 5–6-category demo dictionary works cleanly on PBMC3k's handful of clean populations. At 20 real clusters, several got assigned "Platelet" by argmax with scores barely above zero and negative everywhere else — e.g. cluster 1: T = −0.003, B = −0.040, Monocyte = −0.242, NK = −0.082, Platelet = −0.000, DC = −0.008. "Platelet" wins only because it's the least negative, not because it's a real match to anything.

This is exactly the caveat already on record

docs/pipeline_overview.html section 06 already flags reference-based annotation as sensitive to how well the reference covers the real cell-type space, and explicitly scopes the demo dictionary as PBMC-specific and not general-purpose. This is that caveat showing up concretely: a 6-category hand-picked dictionary was never going to resolve 20 real clusters correctly, and it doesn't. A real annotation pass on this data needs either a much larger curated marker set or a reference-based method (label transfer / scANVI), not an extension of the demo.

05 · Next: full-scale HPC run

What's ready, what's not

  • Environment: envs/environment.yml verified to recreate an identical, functional scrna env both locally (fresh env, re-ran QC, byte-identical results) and on HiPerGator directly.
  • Code: repo synced to /blue/<group>/<user>/scRNA-pipeline/ on HiPerGator.
  • Account: real SLURM account/QoS confirmed directly from HiPerGator (kept in a local, untracked notes file, not published here) — matches what was inferred earlier from the storage path.
  • Status: the full 987,585-cell run has been submitted as a SLURM batch job on HiPerGator once the driver was updated to include the raw-data loading step and re-sized for real scale (128GB/16 CPU/24h vs. the 64GB/8CPU/12h used for local smoke-testing) and smoke-tested end-to-end against the real 50k subset first.
